bib.title: 3. User Experience Design for Agentic Systems (Building Applications with AI Agents)
bib.venue: O'Reilly book chapter (author and year not printed in the PDF text; from the repo's other notes citing Michael Albada, 2025)

question: What design principles make the user experience of agentic systems effective, trustworthy and adoptable across text, GUI, voice and video modalities?
contributions: Autonomy slider (Manual/Ask/Agent) with five design principles
Sync vs async design principles, proactive vs intrusive balance
Context retention, capability communication, uncertainty, clarification, graceful failure, trust

results.claim: Humans speak at 150-180 wpm, read 250-300 wpm and skim above 500 wpm, so voice is slower for dense information.
results.setup: General human speech/reading rates; no study cited
results.quote:
Humans typically speak at 150–180 words per minute, whereas reading
speeds average 250–300 words per minute, with skimming speeds exceed‐
ing 500 words per minute.

results.claim: Example of adaptive autonomy: after 10 successful uses in manual mode the system might suggest assist mode.
results.setup: Illustrative example of an autonomy-slider design principle, not measured
results.quote:
after 10 successful uses in manual mode, the system might
suggest trying assist mode to save time.

results.claim: Autonomy should be exposed as adjustable levels (Manual / Ask / Agent), with transitions, predictable behaviour, stated risks and trust-based suggestions.
results.setup: Design guidance attributed to Karpathy's autonomy slider concept; no data
results.quote: Adapt autonomy based on user trust and competence

results.claim: Graceful failure means transparent acknowledgement, explanation, next steps, preserved progress and escalation to a human.
results.quote:
At its core, graceful failure involves acknowledging the issue transparent‐
ly, offering a helpful explanation, and suggesting actionable next steps.

results.claim: For async tasks: notify at start, give an estimated completion time, deliver a concise summary at the end.
results.quote:
an agent generating an ana‐
lytical report might notify the user when processing begins, provide an
estimated completion time, and deliver a concise, actionable summary
when finished.

results.claim: Hybrid context storage (short-term client side, long-term server side) is said to often give the best UX balance.
results.quote:
A hybrid approach—maintaining
short-term context on the client side for responsiveness and persisting
long-term context on the server side for continuity—often achieves the
best UX balance.

practices: Choose modality by task: text for clear/async/searchable, GUI for structure and multistep workflows, voice for hands-free, video for rich expression (Table 3-1, Interaction Modalities).
Fix text-agent discoverability by listing supported functions in greetings, onboarding, suggestion buttons (Text-Based; Communicating Agent Capabilities).
On an unsupported request offer alternatives or a human hand-off, not a bare rejection (Communicating Agent Capabilities).
Use progressive disclosure and contextual relevance; voice agents list only a few options at a time (Communicating Agent Capabilities).
Let voice agents handle interruptions and mid-sentence corrections; truncate assistant output on user speech (Speech and Voice Interfaces).
Preserve state and context when moving between modalities (Combining Modalities).

Give users an autonomy slider: label levels, enable seamless transitions, predictable behaviour per level, communicate risks, require confirmation before full autonomy on critical tasks, suggest higher autonomy as trust grows (The Autonomy Slider).
Decide up front which experiences are sync and which async so users do not wait on a spinner (Synchronous Versus Asynchronous).
Sync: low latency, brevity, turn-taking, typing indicators, clarifying questions under uncertainty; async: status, ETA, notifications, summaries, retained context (Design Principles sections).
Make proactivity context-aware and user-controllable (frequency, channels, escalation thresholds) (Proactive vs Intrusive).
Persist session state in a database or distributed cache, not only memory; use session id for anonymous users; offer reset of personalization (Maintaining State; Personalization).
Express confidence by explicit statements, visual cues or softer suggestions; avoid overconfidence and excessive hedging; stakes set the transparency level (Communicating Confidence and Uncertainty).
Ask focused, sequenced clarifying questions, referencing earlier answers, explaining why, not too many at once (Asking for Guidance).
Fail gracefully: explain, apologise, give next steps, predefine fallbacks (e.g. voice to text), keep progress, and log failure points to feed back into development (Failing Gracefully).
Be transparent and predictable: same question under same conditions should give same answer, signal unavoidable variability, notify on API loss, never overpromise (Trust in Interaction Design).

terms.definition: allow users to smoothly adjust an agent’s autonomy—from fully manual control to partial automation to fully autonomous operation
dynamically create interface elements, data visualizations, or structured outputs based on user queries
showing core capabilities initially and revealing advanced features as users become more comfortable
synchronous: real-time back-and-forth; asynchronous: agents and users operate independently with intermittent communication
